newsitem.title: RUSSIA: India PM's visit to have arms sales high on agenda.
newsitem.headline: India PM's visit to have arms sales high on agenda.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda starts a two-day visit to Russia on Monday which Moscow hopes will boost the two countries' military and technical cooperation, Interfax news agency said.

Government officials say that arms sales to India, one of Russia's biggest arms clients together with China, will be high on the agenda of a visit which includes talks with President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minster Viktor Chernomyrdin.

Since the mid-1950s Moscow has strongly promoted ties with India, which has been at odds with U.S. ally Pakistan. Moscow has taken part in many of India's major industrial projects and helped equip its armed forces.
Mutual ties have weakened since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, but have begun to stabilise again and have developed well in some areas such as military cooperation.
Interfax quoted the deputy head of Russian arms trader Rosvooruzheniye as saying the two countries were planning to launch a new long-term programme of military cooperation in the year 2000.
The official, Oleg Sidorenko, said the current five-year programme was estimated as worth up to $10 billion.

Detailed figures of Russian-India arms trade are not officially published. But military officials have said that last year's $1.8 billion sale to India of 40 modern SU-30MK jet fighters was the biggest so far.
Russia officially sells arms to 51 countries, but military officials say about 60 percent of sales go to India or China.
Sidorenko said the Russian side was ready to discuss the sale to India of a Russian airforce carrier, the Admiral Gorshkov.
He also said the programme of bilateral military cooperation included Russia's participation in the development of India's air defence, including sales of Russian anti-aircraft systems.
He gave no details. But other Russian officials have said Moscow is keen to sell India some of its C-300 anti-aircraft missile complexes.
A similar deal with Cyprus has triggered a dispute between Nicosia and Turkey, and has incurred charges by U.S. officials that Moscow is upsetting the military balance in the eastern Mediterranean.
